verdict.rationale: Fellow lets workspace admins control which MCP tools an AI assistant/agent can use, revoke connections, and see last-used timestamps (fellow-docs-10, fellow-docs-49, fellow-docs-50), which provides some least-privilege control over what an agent can access. However, the core Developer API key generation process shows no evidence of scoped/permissioned keys (e.g., read-only, resource-specific scopes) — keys appear to be workspace-wide credentials (fellow-docs-16, fellow-docs-2/15), and Super Admin keys grant broad on-behalf-of access rather than narrow scopes (fellow-docs-7, fellow-docs-14). Missing for 10: documented ability to create an API key with restricted scopes/permissions (e.g., read-only vs write, specific endpoint access) rather than just admin-level MCP tool toggling.
